_meta.source: MOE S1 Posting, DSA and PSLE pages; MOE Full SBB secondary school experience and FAQ; SEAB SEC page and 2027 syllabus lists; MOE Post Secondary Admissions Exercise pages; MOE academic calendar and the school terms release for 2027
_meta.notes: Read from the primary MOE and SEAB pages, opened in full, on 2026-11-11. Dates marked 2026 are that cycle's published dates; PSLE results and S1 posting dates are MOE's tentative dates. MOE sets no national dates or marks for a change of level or for choosing upper secondary subjects: it says schools decide at appropriate junctures, on results in the subject and a holistic assessment. Rows marked provisional are school practice and vary by school. Not yet published on 2026-11-11: the 2027 SEC paper dates and the 2027 early admissions dates. The count of examinable subjects a student takes is not stated on any MOE page read, so it is no longer given here.

p6.headline: From PSLE to your first levels
p6.lede: Your PSLE Score sets your Posting Group. A strong AL can let you start that subject at a higher level.

happens.what: Direct School Admission applications, for talents a school recognises. In 2026 they ran from 6 May to 2 June.
PSLE oral in August, then listening and written papers in September. Each subject gets an AL from 1 to 8. Your PSLE Score is the total of four.
Results, the S1 Option Form and the Eligibility Letter. In 2026 that is 24 or 25 November, still tentative. You then have 7 calendar days to list six schools.
Sec 1 posting results. In 2026 that is Friday 18 December, still tentative.

decisions.text: With a score of 21, 22 or 25, choose one of two Posting Groups before listing schools. It applies to all six choices.
List six schools in order. Posting goes by PSLE Score, then citizenship, then choice order, then a ballot.
If an AL allows it, decide whether to start English, Mother Tongue, Maths or Science at a more demanding level.
List your schools in time. With no choices, MOE posts you to a school with places left, by your home address.

student: Which subject do you enjoy most, whatever your AL?
Would you start a subject higher and work hard, or start steady and move up later?
What do you want in a secondary school: a CCA, a programme, friends, distance from home?
parent: Ask: which subject felt easiest this year, and which felt hardest?
Ask: if you could start one subject at a higher level, which would it be?
Ask: what matters to you in a school, apart from the score range?
teacher: Ask the student: what do you do when something is hard?
Ask: which subject would you like to start at a higher level?
Ask: who at home will help you choose your six schools?

p6.source: From the MOE S1 Posting, DSA and PSLE pages, read 11 November 2026.

sec1.headline: Settling in, and the first review
sec1.lede: English, Mother Tongue, Maths, Science and Humanities each sit at G1, G2 or G3. A level can move up, with your school.

happens.what: About a third of the week is in a mixed form class. Subjects: Art, Music, Design and Technology, Food and Consumer Education, PE and CCE. These have no levels.
For levelled subjects, you join students from other classes at the same level.
Levels change at junctures your school sets. It looks at your results in the subject and your overall workload. Schools usually explain their criteria at a briefing early in the year.
Your aptitude for and interest in Geography, History and Literature this year decide if they move up in Sec 2. From G1, schools look at English and G1 Humanities.

decisions.text: Whether to take a subject at a more demanding level, if your school offers it. Each school sets its own criteria, so ask your teacher.
Which CCA to commit to. A CCA is compulsory in secondary school, and CCA bonus points count in post secondary admission.

student: Which subject could you move up by the end of the year? What would your teacher want to see?
Which subject needs more of your time, without changing its level?
Which Humanities subject do you enjoy enough to work harder at next year?
parent: Ask: which subject could go up a level? What would help?
Ask: is any subject taking so much time that the others suffer?
Ask: what does your teacher say you do well?
teacher: Ask the student: which subject would you like to try at the next level?
Ask: what does a good week of revision look like for you?
Ask: which Humanities subject do you look forward to?

sec1.source: From the MOE Full SBB pages and FAQ, read 11 November 2026.

sec2.headline: The year that shapes Sec 3
sec2.lede: Humanities can move up now. Before Sec 3 you choose your upper secondary subjects, guided by your school.

happens.what: Humanities moves earned in Sec 1 take effect.
Applied Learning Modules at a polytechnic or ITE open to you. You can take up to 3 during secondary school.
Many schools brief families on upper secondary subjects during Sec 2. Ask your school for its dates.
Your school guides your subject choices. It looks at your learning progress and needs.

decisions.text: Your Sec 3 subjects: English, Mother Tongue, Mathematics, Science, Humanities and electives. On mainly G1 subjects, you take Computing or Science.
Science: Science at G1, a Science pair at G2 or G3, or Physics, Chemistry and Biology at G3.
Humanities at G2 or G3: Social Studies with Geography, History or Literature. You can add a full Humanities subject. At G1, Humanities is not examined.
Additional Mathematics at G2 or G3, if your school offers it to you. Each school sets its own criteria.

student: Which subjects do you want in Sec 3 because you like them?
Which subject is close to moving up before your Sec 3 subjects are set?
Which places do you want to keep open, and which subjects keep them open?
parent: Ask: which subjects would you choose if it were only up to you?
Ask: which subject is close to the next level? What would help?
Ask: would you rather take more subjects, or fewer done well?
teacher: Ask the student: which subject are you choosing for yourself?
Ask: which level do you want to keep or raise by the end of the year?
Ask: is Additional Maths, or a pure science, right for you? Why?

sec2.source: From the MOE Full SBB pages and the SEAB subject lists, read 11 November 2026. Each school sets its own dates.

sec3.headline: Your combination, year one
sec3.lede: Your upper secondary subjects start. A level can still change, with your school. Grade targets start to matter.

happens.what: The first of two years that lead to the SEC examination.
A level can still change. An elective can drop a level if you wish. For English, Mother Tongue, Mathematics, Science or Humanities, your school assesses first.

decisions.text: Set a grade target for each subject. The Targets tab shows the score each place reads.
Whether any level should change for Sec 4. The school decides, and a change is not guaranteed.

student: Which grade target is a stretch, but still realistic for you?
Which subject takes the most time for the least progress? Why?
Which place are you aiming for, and what score does it read?
parent: Ask: what grade would you be proud of in each subject?
Ask: which subject needs help that we could find together?
Ask: what are you aiming for after Sec 4, for now?
teacher: Ask the student: which target would you set yourself?
Ask: what one habit would raise your weakest grade by one step?
Ask: which place are you working towards? Do you know what it counts?

sec3.source: From the MOE Full SBB FAQ, read 11 November 2026. Each school sets its own dates.

sec4.headline: Finishing well, and the SEC
sec4.lede: The first SEC is in 2027. Early admissions can offer you a place before the results.

happens.what: Early admissions, before the exams. In 2026, ITE applications were in late May and polytechnic applications in late June. DSA for JC opened in May, with dates set by each JC.
Orals, listening and science practicals.
Check your CCA record with your school. CCA bonus points count in the Post Secondary Admissions Exercise.
English and Mother Tongue written papers. Mother Tongue has one written sitting a year, at every level.
All other written papers.
All SEC results on one day. The Post Secondary Admissions Exercise opens the same day and runs for six days.
You rank up to 12 courses on one portal, across JC, MI, polytechnic, PFP and ITE.
Posting results. For the first SEC cohort that is early February 2028.

decisions.text: Whether to apply through early admissions, and for which courses. Polytechnic takes up to 3 choices. You can accept one offer only.
Your choices in the Post Secondary Admissions Exercise, in order. On a tied score, citizenship counts first and then choice order.
If Sec 5 is open to you, whether to take it, and what to aim for.

student: Which course would you apply for in early admissions? What would you show them?
Which two grades would change your score the most?
If your results are different from what you expect, what is your second choice?
parent: Ask: which course would you apply for early, if you could?
Ask: what is your plan if results are better or worse than you hope?
Ask: what help do you need between now and October?
teacher: Ask the student: which course interests you most? Have you visited it?
Ask: which two subjects will you put extra hours into, and when?
Ask: what would you choose if your score came in two points higher or lower?

sec4.source: From the SEAB SEC page and the MOE admissions pages, read 11 November 2026. The 2027 dates were not yet published.

sec5.headline: A fifth year, aimed at something
sec5.lede: Sec 5 gives you another year, and subjects can move up a level. It helps most when you aim it at one place.

happens.what: 3 or more G3 passes, without qualifying for JC, MI or Year 1 of polytechnic.
2 or fewer G3 passes, with ELMAB3 of 21 or better, or ELB3 or MAB3 of 14 or better. Scores are worked out at G2, and each subject counted needs Grade 5 or better.
To take every subject at G3 in Sec 5, you need ELMAB3 of 19 or better.
SEC papers in the subjects you take, then the Post Secondary Admissions Exercise. Results from two exam years can be combined.

decisions.text: Which subjects to take, and at which level, to reach the place you are aiming for.
Whether the Polytechnic Foundation Programme or a 2 year Higher Nitec suits you better than Sec 5.

student: Which place are you aiming for this year?
Which subject moving to G3 would make the biggest difference?
Would another route get you there sooner? Would you prefer it?
parent: Ask: what do you want this extra year to make possible?
Ask: which subject would you take to G3, and what help do you need?
Ask: have we compared PFP and Higher Nitec side by side?
teacher: Ask the student: what place is this year for?
Ask: which subject at G3 is realistic for you? How will you study it differently?
Ask: what would make you choose a different route?

sec5.source: From the MOE Full SBB page on the SEC and the fifth year, read 11 November 2026.
